description_ru: Как мексиканская художница превратила болезнь и травму в яркое и узнаваемое искусство.
text:
Frida Kahlo was born in 1907 in Mexico City, in a house that was later called the Blue House. When she was six, she caught polio, and one of her legs stayed thinner than the other. Other children laughed at her, but Frida grew up strong and curious. She wanted to become a doctor.

Everything changed in 1925. At the age of eighteen, Frida was travelling on a bus when it crashed into a tram. She broke her back, her leg and several other bones, and she spent months in bed. To help her pass the time, her parents made a special easel and put a mirror above her bed. Frida started to paint herself. If she had not had the accident, she might never have become an artist.

Over the years, she painted many self-portraits, because, as she explained, she was often alone, and she knew herself best. Her pictures are full of bright colours, animals, flowers and symbols from Mexican culture. In 1929 she married the famous painter Diego Rivera. Their relationship was stormy, but they supported each other's work.

Frida suffered pain all her life and had many operations. Still, she kept painting until the end. She died in 1954 at the age of forty-seven. Today her paintings are loved all over the world, and the Blue House is a museum.
